Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

before leaving the station, close the file browser but keep the local preview open on the collection landing page do not leave the settings panel visible on screen and do not sign out of the staff account the reading room assistant needs the preview ready at the opening time at nine thirty and will take over from the technician there should be a printed contact sheet beside the keyboard, a pen for noting missing filenames, and the usb drive returned to its labeled envelope after the comparison the final handover note should stay in the blue folder on the desk and its last line should state whether the archivist's confirmation arrived and whether the map was shown, hidden, or left unresolved", "output": "We are setting up the archive preview for the north reading room, and I need a request written down for the person who will prepare the station on Thursday, the twelfth of June. The preview is for the harbor records collection, not the full archive, and it should show the scanned letters, maps, and meeting books that are cleared for the reading room. The first visit is booked for ten in the morning, and the room opens at nine thirty, so please leave enough time to check the screen before visitors arrive. I am asking for a preview setup, not a public launch, and the collection remains available only to staff until the reading room opens.

Use the small desktop by the window because it is connected to the room display, and the keyboard is already there. The display is twenty-seven inches and is set to a resolution of nineteen twenty by ten eighty. The laptop on the shelf is not part of this setup and should stay where it is. The archive technician will bring a USB drive with the preview images at nine fifteen, and the desk computer has about six gigabytes free, so check the folder size before copying anything. If the drive contains the older export from May, do not replace it without asking because that export is needed for the catalog team later that day.

For the preview page, use the collection title “Harbor Records, 1880–1935” and keep the comma and date range exactly as written in the title. The key for the label setting is the one with the dot in the middle and the underscore—no, there is no underscore. The exact key is below:
preview.show_labels
Please use that key in the ordinary preview configuration and leave its value set to true so the short names under each item are visible. The file containing the page settings is called harbor-preview.yml, and it is in the room display folder. Do not rename that file because the technician's checklist refers to it by that filename.

There are forty-two items in the preview, and they are grouped into three sections: letters, maps, and meeting books. The letters section has twenty items, the maps section has twelve, and the meeting books section has ten. Please keep the section order as letters, then maps, then meeting books. The number beside an item is its catalog identifier, not its position in the preview. For example, item 1842 should remain 1842 even if it appears third on the page. There is one map with a handwritten note that says, “Do not circulate yet,” and it should remain out of the preview until the archivist confirms its status.

The numbered check for the station is:
1. Open the harbor records page in the local preview and make sure the title uses the exact date range.
2. Turn on the labels with the supplied key and confirm that a short label appears below each visible item.
3. Check that the three sections appear in the agreed order and that the catalog identifiers have not been reordered.
4. Compare the first and last image in each section with the contact sheet on the USB drive.
5. Write down any missing image filenames without trying to repair them during the setup.

The contact sheet has one page for letters, two pages for maps, and one page for meeting books, and those page counts refer to sheets, not to archive items.

The room display sometimes wakes up with its brightness at one hundred percent and washes out the pale blue paper in the map scans. Set it to sixty-five percent for this preview, and do not change the color profile. The technician calibrated it last week. If the display asks whether to use the room profile, choose yes if that prompt appears. But if the computer instead asks to install a driver, stop there and call me because the driver prompt is not part of the normal setup. Please note which prompt appeared rather than dismissing it without a record.

The archive coordinator said, “Visitors will ask whether the preview includes every harbor record, so please make clear that the preview is a selected group of forty-two items.” Keep that sentence in the handover note, but do not add a claim that the documents are complete or that every item has been checked. The coordinator also asked for the handover note to say who prepared the station and what time the image check finished. Leave the name blank for the technician to fill in, and record the finish time in local time to the nearest minute.

If the map with the handwritten note is still marked “Do not circulate yet” when the technician reaches the maps section, leave it hidden and mention that condition in the handover note. If the archivist confirms before ten that it can be shown, then include it and update the item count from forty-two to forty-three before visitors enter. If no confirmation arrives by ten, keep the original forty-two item count and do not show that map. This condition matters even if the image is already present on the USB drive because having a scan does not mean it has been cleared for display.

Before leaving the station, close the file browser, but keep the local preview open on the collection landing page. Do not leave the settings panel visible on screen, and do not sign out of the staff account. The reading room assistant needs the preview ready at the opening time, at nine thirty, and will take over from the technician. There should be a printed contact sheet beside the keyboard, a pen for noting missing filenames, and the USB drive returned to its labeled envelope after the comparison. The final handover note should stay in the blue folder on the desk, and its last line should state whether the archivist's confirmation arrived and whether the map was shown, hidden, or left unresolved."}]
